one_liner: QuickBooks Online has a broad REST accounting API with self-serve OAuth 2.0, a free developer account, sandbox and a free Builder tier. A production app assessment may apply, and the pages don't confirm it.
auth_notes: Authorization-code OAuth 2.0 per company (realmId). The token lifetime details in the draft are not verified on the fetched pages.
access_notes: A free Intuit developer account gives a client ID and secret plus a free sandbox company. All apps are auto-enrolled in the free Builder tier, which has 500k CorePlus credits a month. The FAQ mentions an app assessment questionnaire as a tier requirement, but the fetched text is truncated and doesn't say whether Builder needs it.
blocker_notes: Builder tier CorePlus calls are capped at 500k a month and blocked above that. Premium APIs need a paid tier. Dev and sandbox work is immediate.

evidence.quote: Each of your clients' QuickBooks Online companies will need to individually connect and authorize your app through OAuth 2.0, since access is scoped per company
This generates your client ID and client secret, plus a free sandbox company for testing.
All apps are automatically enrolled in the Intuit App Partner Program at the Builder tier.
To jumpstart your development, use [Intuit Developer Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbo/docs/mcp-connector), an AI-enabled development environment.
The Accounting API covers the core entities you'd need for a consolidated dashboard: invoices, bills, payments, customers, vendors, accounts, and journal entries
